recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No current FHIR-core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-11235; if MolecularDefinition implementers need tighter coordinate-system semantics, handle that through a MolecularDefinition-specific Clinical Genomics issue.
issue_request: FHIR-11235 was a Published/Persuasive Clinical Genomics change request for the DSTU2 FHIR-core Sequence resource. It observed that Sequence.coordinateSystem was an integer and asked for stronger guidance or constraint to valid 0-based and 1-based choices; the final resolution said the integer could not then be constrained to only 0 and 1, so explanatory sections and examples would be added.
initial_application: Commit d830ddede2fa70d5f6ccca85e723caa4a2c7a7bf applied the issue to the then-current source/sequence spreadsheet by updating Sequence.coordinateSystem to describe 0 for 0-based inclusive-start/exclusive-end coordinates and 1 for 1-based inclusive-start/inclusive-end coordinates. Historical release3 and release4 generated/profile artifacts preserve that wording for Sequence and MolecularSequence.
additional_context: Current source/fhir.ini lists Sequence under removed resources, comments out molecularsequence, and keeps moleculardefinition as the active Clinical Genomics source. Later FHIR-22762 work moved MolecularSequence.coordinateSystem away from a top-level integer to a relative CodeableConcept bound to the LOINC coordinate-system value set, and later FHIR-51227 work replaced MolecularSequence with MolecularDefinition. Current MolecularDefinition uses coordinateInterval coordinate-system CodeableConcepts and external molecular data type profiles rather than the old integer element.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit on the combined branch. Porting the retired Sequence integer 0/1 wording into MolecularDefinition would be a new MolecularDefinition modeling decision, not a reconciliation of FHIR-11235.
